no-shared-memory.reason: isolane removes SharedArrayBuffer and Atomics (no shared-memory timers for side channels), so tests that build one fail.

no-wasm.reason: WebAssembly is off unless an isolate enables `wasm`; these tests use WebAssembly.Memory to make buffers, and this run leaves it off.

not-worker-scope.reason: The global is a plain ECMAScript global with the WinterTC APIs, not a browser WorkerGlobalScope, which idlharness.js requires to start.

tentative-owning-streams.reason: Tentative "owning" streams and transfer lists, not in the Streams standard yet; isolane implements the published standards.

webcrypto-drafts.reason: Algorithms from WICG drafts beyond the W3C Web Cryptography standard: Modern Algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, ChaCha20-Poly1305, AES-OCB, KMAC, Argon2, SHA-3, SHAKE, cSHAKE, TurboSHAKE, KangarooTwelve, getPublicKey, encapsulate/decapsulate, SubtleCrypto.supports) and Secure Curves' Ed448. isolane's crypto.subtle is Deno's JS from before Deno added them (plus X448); they're on the roadmap.

no-xhr.reason: XMLHttpRequest is a browser API; WinterTC runtimes (isolane, Deno, workerd) provide fetch instead.

no-cache-api.reason: The Cache API (`caches`) is browser storage, not part of WinterTC's minimum common API.

no-video-frame.reason: VideoFrame (WebCodecs) is a browser media API.

forbidden-headers.reason: Forbidden request headers and method-override headers protect a browser user's session; server runtimes (Deno, workerd) let code set them, and so does isolane.

cors-and-origin.reason: CORS, the no-cors/same-origin modes, opaque responses, and the Origin header enforce the same-origin policy between a page's origin and others; there's no page origin to protect here (as in Deno and workerd).

referrer.reason: Referrer policy derives the Referer header from a document; isolane sends none (as Deno and workerd).

manual-redirect.reason: With redirect: 'manual', isolane returns the real 3xx response (as Deno and workerd), not an opaque-redirect filtered for a page's cross-origin protection.

http-cache.reason: No HTTP cache: server runtimes go to the network every time (cache modes are accepted and ignored), so cache hit counts differ.

set-cookie.reason: Set-Cookie is readable from response headers (as in Deno and workerd); browsers hide it from scripts.

request-window.reason: RequestInit's `window` only means something with a browsing context.

no-canvas.reason: OffscreenCanvas and ImageBitmap are browser graphics APIs, not part of WinterTC's minimum common API (nor in Deno or workerd).

secure-context.reason: In a browser, crypto.subtle, SubtleCrypto, and CryptoKey exist only in secure contexts (https pages); a server runtime has no insecure context, so they're always there (as in Deno, Node, and workerd).

no-tls.reason: The WPT server here runs without TLS, so https URLs don't connect.

no-h2.reason: No HTTP/2 server in the harness; .h2 tests need one.

node-http-parser.reason: The broker's HTTP client (Node's) refuses response bytes Fetch allows (control characters in header values, bare LF line endings in .asis responses); isolane keeps Node's strict parser rather than loosening how it parses untrusted servers.

http2-retry.reason: Retrying a 421 on a new connection is HTTP/2 connection-coalescing behaviour of a browser's network stack.

wpt-proxy.reason: Uses WPT's proxy for a fake host (bad-port.wpt), which this harness doesn't run; the fetch policy also refuses that host.

encoding-edge.reason: After a fatal streaming error, the Encoding Standard keeps the byte that ended a malformed sequence when the decoder had to look at it (EUC-JP's JIS0212 case: the ASCII byte is "restored to the queue") and drops the rest of the input. encoding_rs's fatal API reports the error the same way in both cases (the byte is left unread either way), so the op can't tell them apart without per-encoding rules. Deno's op is the same; an upstream encoding_rs API that says whether the byte was examined would fix it.

url-crate.reason: The `url` crate (as in Deno) lags the newest URL-standard changes: spaces before ?/# in opaque paths, file URLs with Windows drive letters and backslashes, xn-- hosts, blob: origins, some setters. ada (Node's parser) gets all of these right (WPT's urltestdata 896/896 vs 831, setters 277/278 vs 255) but is 1.1 MB of C++ parsing guest strings outside the V8 sandbox, so it stays unadopted for now (roadmap: URL parser).

event-attrs.reason: Deno's vendored Event: timeStamp is always 0 (and under isolane's frozen clock performance.now() is often still 0 when an event is made, so these timeStamp > 0 checks couldn't pass reliably anyway), and isTrusted is one accessor on Event.prototype instead of a [LegacyUnforgeable] own property of each event, Deno's deliberate trade for faster event creation.

empty-formdata.reason: An empty FormData body is the closing boundary alone (Deno's formDataToBlob), so text() isn't empty. Serializing it as nothing, as this test wants, would break fetch/api/body/formdata.any.js, which parses that body back into an empty FormData, while an empty multipart body must still fail to parse (response-consume-empty's "formData with correct multipart type (error case)"): the tests can't all pass.

then-injection.reason: Reading a body resolves promises with its bytes (a Uint8Array), so a patched Object.prototype.then sees, and can replace, them; the Streams and Fetch standards' internal reads never resolve a promise with an object. Same in Deno; fixing it means reworking how Deno's body and stream code returns results.

streams-edge.reason: Two Streams edge cases in Deno's vendored implementation (same in Deno): a patched Object.prototype.then runs before a BYOB enqueue() has committed every pending read (the then-injection class, see then-injection), and when transformer.cancel() calls controller.error() during a pending writable.close(), the writable side is still erroring rather than errored when the cancel algorithm settles, so readable.cancel() resolves instead of rejecting.

tentative-urlpattern.reason: Tentative URLPattern additions, not in the URL Pattern standard yet: URLPattern.compareComponent() and generate(). Deno lacks them too.

urlpattern-v-flag.reason: The URL Pattern standard now compiles regexp groups with the `v` flag (set operations like `[[a-z]--a]`); the `urlpattern` crate (0.4.2, as Deno uses) still generates regexps for the `u` flag, which `v` rejects (it requires `/` escaped in classes). Needs the crate to follow the spec; Deno fails the same subtests.
